messages:
jamie: Heads-up — customer reported reproducible SSE stream drop mid-token when phone sleeps then wakes and switches from cellular -> WiFi. They get a partial last event and then client stops receiving. Ticket: #INC-3821. Repro steps and logs below.

liam: Thanks — any pattern on carrier or OS? Android/iOS? SDK version?

jamie: Android only so far (Pixel 6, Android 13). SDK v1.4.3. Happens with both Verizon and T-Mobile during handoffs. Repro: lock screen for ~20s, reopen, switch networks manually, app resumes and attempts reconnect. Sometimes reconnect works, often we see partial frame then dead.

anika: Can you paste the client logs + the raw SSE payload we got?

jamie: Pasting minimal logs (redacted):
```
[2024-09-15T18:21:03.482Z] SSEClient: connected, session_id=abcd-1234
[2024-09-15T18:21:15.900Z] SSEClient: onmessage -> {"delta":"...some tokens..."}
[2024-09-15T18:21:16.102Z] SSEClient: onmessage -> {"delta":"partial-token"}
[2024-09-15T18:21:16.105Z] Network: got EVENT: data: {"content":"...partial"}\n\n// phone goes to lock/sleep, then network flips
[2024-09-15T18:21:36.710Z] Connectivity: cell->wifi
[2024-09-15T18:21:36.812Z] SSEClient: onerror -> java.io.IOException: stream closed (code=1006)
[2024-09-15T18:21:36.815Z] SSEClient: reconnecting (attempt 1) with token refreshed
[2024-09-15T18:21:36.920Z] HTTP: POST /v1/streams?model=x-large headers: {Authorization: Bearer <token>} -> 401 Unauthorized
```

jamie: The server returned 401 on the immediate reconnect attempt while the client thought it had a fresh token. Sometimes server logs show a 200 then connection immediately closed with `RST`. Partial payloads are consistently present (client gets incomplete JSON).

support-bot: Incident rule matched: possible client-midstream-reconnect pattern. Suggested tags: `sse`, `mobile`, `network-handovers`, `auth`.

liam: Interesting — two hypotheses: 1) token refresh race means the new token not propagated to backend routing (LB auth cache) causing 401; 2) NAT/reverse proxy resets kill in-flight connections and the client library doesn't re-request missed bytes (no Last-Event-ID usage). Which SDK version handles `Last-Event-ID`?

anika: SDK v1.4.3 does not auto-send Last-Event-ID right now. We added it in v1.5.0 behind a flag. Also we recently tightened token TTLs for streaming tokens to 30s. Could be interacting with quick reconnects after sleep.

cheng: Can we correlate server-side stream-session for `session_id=abcd-1234`? Need logs from the runtime side (ingress LB, auth plugin, runtime worker). Also grep for `RST` or `connection reset by peer` around 2024-09-15T18:21:36.

ryan-eng: I'll pull runtime logs. Quick note: we saw a spike in `connection reset` from envoy when mobile devices transition networks — NAT pinhole expiry ~20s is common. We add TCP keepalives but SSE over HTTP/1.1 doesn't always survive NAT rebinding.

jamie: Repro steps we gave to the customer (concise):
1) Open chat on cellular (start streaming generation).
2) Wait until partial tokens emitted.
3) Lock phone for 20s.
4) Unlock and toggle WiFi on to force cell->wifi handoff.
5) Watch client hit reconnect and either get 401 or silent stop.

anika: Immediate mitigations for support to propose to customer:
- Upgrade SDK to v1.5.0-beta which sends Last-Event-ID and will resume from last event id (best-effort).
- Increase client reconnect backoff to 500ms -> 2s jitter to avoid auth TTL races.
- Ensure SDK refreshes token and waits for token update before reconnect attempt (race guard).

liam: Server-side mitigations we can try: accept reconnects with a `stream-resume` query param for a short window (60s) without re-auth if session cookie matches, or allow `Last-Event-ID` header to resume without requiring full re-auth. Both need security review.

cheng: For now, I hooked the ingress logs and found this for session abcd-1234 (snip):
```
ingress[18:21:36.900] -> auth: token check ok
runtime[18:21:36.905] -> worker: accepted connection, session=abcd-1234
runtime[18:21:36.907] -> worker: connection closed by peer (RST)
```
No explicit 401 in runtime, the 401 jamie saw was from the auth layer earlier on a later reconnect attempt.

ryan-eng: Action items:
- ryan-eng: attach pcap from customer's device (request) and correlate timings.
- cheng: add trace id search for `abcd-1234` across LB/auth/runtime and share cutoff timestamps.
- anika: prepare SDK patch to gate immediate reconnect until token refresh completes and publish a beta to the customer.
- liam: draft a recommended support reply with mitigations and repro confirmation steps.

jamie: Customer asked if there's anything to change server-side short-term while we prepare SDK patch. They prefer a server config toggle if possible.

cheng: Short-term server option: enable `sse-heartbeat` which sends a `:hb\n\n` comment every 15s to keep NAT pinhole open. That should reduce RSTs during short sleeps. Can be toggled per-customer route. Security: no auth change.

anika: I'll add the heartbeat toggle to the console as an emergency knob (low-risk) and publish guidance.

liam: Also note: ask customer to try toggling keep-alive headers on the OS side if possible, and try a longer open time before lock to see if NAT expiry is the main culprit.

jamie: I'll send the patch link and the heartbeat toggle to the customer and request pcap. I'll post updates here after they test. :thumbsup:
